title: Protocol for the generation of blastocyst-like structures from mouse extended pluripotent stem cells
protocol: Dissociate EPS colonies on MEFs: Aspirate medium and wash cells with DPBS once.
Add TrypLE (Thermo Fisher Scientific, 1 mL/10 cm² area) to cells and incubate the plate at 37°C for about 3 min.
Check cells under a microscope to ensure that cells are mostly detached; if not, extend the incubation time.
Add CDF12 medium in an equal volume of TrypLE and pipette up and down several times to resuspend cells.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min and remove supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL EPS medium.
Transfer cell resuspension to a gelatin-coated 6-well plate and incubate at 37°C for 1 h (MEF cells attach faster than EPS cells).
Check the plate under a microscope after 1 hour to ensure most MEFs are depleted from the suspension.
Collect cell suspension and filter it through a 45 μm cell strainer to eliminate cell aggregates.
Count cells using the Bio-Rad TC-10 counter or a hemocytometer.
Calculate the volume for the required number of cells.
Seed dissociated EPS cells into microwells for the formation of small cell aggregates and subsequently EPS-blastoids.
Mix cells with medium, and pipette 500 μL into each well of the AggreWell 400 24-well plate or 2 mL for the AggreWell 400 6-well plate.
Shake the plate back and forth or from left to right.
Spin down the plate at 200 g for 2 minutes.
Check cells under a microscope to ensure they are evenly distributed in all microwells.
Pipette several times with a wide bore pipette tip if cells are not evenly distributed, then centrifuge again.
Remove medium by tilting the plate slightly and aspirating with a P200 tip gently placed against the edge between the side and bottom of the wells.
Replace removed medium with blastoid induction medium (500 μL for AggreWell 400 24-well plate).
Monitor the culture daily for EPS-blastoids emerging from Day 3 to Day 5.
Identify EPS-blastoids as cavitated sphere-like structures, round or near-round shaped, with diameters of 60–170 μm.
Transfer EPS-blastoid culture into a 6-well plate for picking.
Use wide-bore pipette tips to gently pipette up and down to blow off the blastoid from microwells.
Pick up EPS-Blastoids using a hand-pulled glass microcapillary pipettes.
Pre-wet the glass pipette with 1% BSA in PBS.
Place pooled EPS-Blastoids into two drops of PBS successively for washing.
Transfer the EPS-Blastoid into a drop of 4% PFA for fixation and further immunostaining analysis.
Store fixed EPS-Blastoids in PBS at 4°C for months if needed.
Transfer EPS-blastoids onto an ibidi μ-plate for further culturing using the IVC1/IVC2 or similar culture system.
Pick up EPS-blastoids manually and transfer them into a KSOM drop using a mouth pipette.
Anesthetize ICR female surrogate mice at 2.5 days post coitum with ketamine and xylazine dissolved in saline.
Expose the uterine horn surgically.
Puncture the uterine horn with a 27G needle.
Wash EPS-blastoids three times in KSOM drops.
Load EPS-blastoids into the pipette.
Transfer EPS-blastoids to the uterine horn through the puncture site.
Inject Evans Blue into the tail vein of the surrogate mice and wait for 15 minutes before performing C-section.
Dissect out the uterus from the surrogate mice at 6.5, 7.5, or 8.5 days post coitum.
Dissect embryo-like structures out of the deciduae.
Fix tissue samples with 4% PFA overnight (14-16 hours).
Embed fixed tissue samples in O.C.T compound.
Cut frozen sections (10 μm thick) using a microtome cryostat.
Store sections at -20°C or lower for months if not immediately needed for immunostaining.
Perform immunostaining on the sections.
